summary: This bill bans all weather modification activities in the US by making it a federal crime (with fines up to $100,000 and up to 5 years in prison) to knowingly release chemicals, biological agents, or pollutants into the atmosphere to alter weather or climate, repeals all existing federal permits or authorities for such activities, bars federal agencies and grantees from researching or conducting them, and requires FAA and EPA systems for reporting and investigating violations.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes new federal reporting systems (via FAA and EPA), mandates investigations of suspected violations, and requires coordination across multiple agencies. These provisions create modest new administrative and enforcement functions, implying a small expansion of government activity and spending. Repeal of existing weather modification authorities may offset this slightly, but the net effect is a minor increase in spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, credits, or revenue collection.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare delivery, insurance, public health programs, or medical regulation.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, gun ownership, or gun regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, visas, border security, or immigrant protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion access, reproductive rights, or related regulations.

The bill contains no provisions that directly alter military or defense budgets, programs, or authorities, though weather modification has historically had military applications; the text does not engage this dimension.

The bill explicitly prohibits a wide range of atmospheric interventions (geoengineering, cloud seeding, stratospheric aerosol injection, marine cloud brightening, solar radiation modification) and repeals all existing federal authorizations for such activities. It adds new regulatory enforcement mechanisms under the EPA and FAA framed around air quality and atmospheric composition. This constitutes a substantial expansion of environmental regulation and protections against climate-related technological interventions.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, unemployment benefits, or other safety-net entitlements.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, education funding, curriculum, or school choice.
The bill contains no provisions related to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement policy.

The bill creates new federal criminal penalties (up to $100,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment) and civil penalties for violations, plus requirements for DOJ referral. This adds to federal enforcement authority, representing a modest shift toward stricter penalties and policing in the specific domain of atmospheric activities.
The bill contains no provisions related to tariffs, trade agreements, import/export rules, or globalization.
The bill contains no provisions that directly address deficits, debt ceilings, or fiscal policy priorities.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.

The bill contains no provisions related to data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance oversight.
The bill contains no provisions related to workers' rights, union organizing, or employer obligations.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination law.
